definitions.english: A budget is a plan for your money.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso ke moralo wa chelete ya hao.

definitions.english: Budgeting means deciding where your money will go.
definitions.sesotho: Ho etsa tekanyetso ho bolela ho etsa qeto ya hore na chelete e ya kae.

definitions.english: A budget is like a map for your money.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e tshwana le mmapa wa chelete ya hao.

definitions.english: When you budget, you divide your money into different purposes.
definitions.sesotho: Ha o etsa tekanyetso, o arola chelete ka merero e fapaneng.

definitions.english: A budget helps you know how much to spend, save, and give.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e o thusa ho tseba hore na o sebedisa, o boloka le ho fana bokae.

definitions.english: Budgeting is creating a structured plan for income and expenses.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso ke ho theha moralo o hlophisitsweng wa moputso le ditshenyehelo.

definitions.english: A budget tracks money coming in and going out.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e latela chelete e kenang le e tswang.

definitions.english: Budgeting means allocating income to different categories.
definitions.sesotho: Ho etsa tekanyetso ho bolela ho arola moputso ka dikarolo tse fapaneng.

definitions.english: A budget helps you live within your means.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e o thusa ho phela ka hara seo o nang le sona.

definitions.english: Budgeting involves comparing income to expenses.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e kenyelletsa ho bapisa moputso le ditshenyehelo.

definitions.english: Budgeting is the systematic allocation of financial resources.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso ke ho arola mehlodi ya lichelete ka mokgwa o hlophisitsweng.

definitions.english: A budget matches income against fixed and variable expenses.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e bapisa moputso le ditshenyehelo tse sa fetoheng le tse fetohang.
Tekanyetso e kenyelletsa mekgwa ya zero-based le 50/30/20.

definitions.english: Effective budgeting requires understanding cash flow.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e atlehileng e hloka ho utlwisisa phallo ya chelete.

definitions.english: Budgeting provides visibility and control over every Maloti.
definitions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e fana ka ponahalo le taolo hodima Maloti a mang le a mang.

examples.english: You get M50: M20 snacks, M20 savings, M10 giving.
examples.sesotho: O fumana M50: M20 dipompong, M20 poloko, M10 ho fana.

examples.english: Your budget shows M30. A toy costs M40. You need M10 more.
examples.sesotho: Tekanyetso e bontsha M30. Sebapadiswa se bitsa M40. O hloka M10 e nngwe.

examples.english: Divide M100 into three envelopes: Spend, Save, Give.
examples.sesotho: Arola M100 ka di-enfelopo tse tharo: Sebedisa, Boloka, Fana.

examples.english: Check your budget before buying anything.
examples.sesotho: Hlahloba tekanyetso ya hao pele o reka letho.

examples.english: Weekly budget: M15 transport, M10 food, M5 saving.
examples.sesotho: Tekanyetso ya beke: M15 dipalangwang, M10 dijo, M5 poloko.

examples.english: Monthly M600: M200 transport, M150 food, M100 airtime, M100 savings, M50 fun.
examples.sesotho: Ka kgwedi M600: M200 dipalangwang, M150 dijo, M100 airtime, M100 poloko, M50 boithabiso.

examples.english: Earn M500, expenses M450, M50 left to save.
examples.sesotho: Fumana M500, ditshenyehelo M450, M50 e setseng ho boloka.

examples.english: Use envelopes: M200 food, M100 transport, M50 savings.
examples.sesotho: Sebedisa di-enfelopo: M200 dijo, M100 dipalangwang, M50 poloko.

examples.english: Cut entertainment from M150 to M50 to balance budget.
examples.sesotho: Fokotsa boithabiso ho tloha M150 ho ya M50 ho lekalekanya tekanyetso.

examples.english: Track spending for one month to understand patterns.
examples.sesotho: Latela tshebediso kgwedi e le nngwe ho utlwisisa mekgwa.

examples.english: Bursary M2,500: M1,000 rent, M800 food, M300 transport, M200 books, M200 savings.
examples.sesotho: Bursary M2,500: M1,000 rente, M800 dijo, M300 dipalangwang, M200 dibuka, M200 poloko.

examples.english: Zero-based: every Maloti of M3,000 has a job.
examples.sesotho: Zero-based: Maloti a mang le a mang a M3,000 a na le mosebetsi.

examples.english: 50/30/20 on M4,000: M2,000 needs, M1,200 wants, M800 savings.
examples.sesotho: 50/30/20 ho M4,000: M2,000 ditlhoko, M1,200 ditakatso, M800 poloko.

examples.english: Reduce eating out from M600 to M300 to save M300 more.
examples.sesotho: Fokotsa ho jella kantle ho tloha M600 ho ya M300 ho boloka M300 e nngwe.

examples.english: Allocate 10 percent of income to emergency fund.
examples.sesotho: Arola 10% ya moputso ho letlole la tshohanyetso.

misconceptions.english: Budgets are boring — FALSE! Budgets help you get what you want.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ditekanyetso di a tena — HA SE NNETE! Di o thusa ho fumana seo o se batlang.

misconceptions.english: Only adults need budgets — FALSE! Children can plan money too.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba baholo feela ba hlokang ditekanyetso — HA SE NNETE! Bana le bona ba ka rera.

misconceptions.english: A budget means you cannot buy anything — FALSE! It means buying what matters.
misconceptions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e bolela hore o ke ke wa reka letho — HA SE NNETE! E bolela ho reka se bohlokwa.

misconceptions.english: Budgeting is only for people struggling — FALSE! Everyone benefits.
misconceptions.sesotho: Tekanyetso ke ya batho ba nang le mathata feela — HA SE NNETE! Bohle ba a rua molemo.

misconceptions.english: Budgets are too restrictive — FALSE! They give freedom within limits.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ditekanyetso di a thibela — HA SE NNETE! Di fana ka tokoloho ka hara meedi.

misconceptions.english: You need lots of money to budget — FALSE! Works with any amount.
misconceptions.sesotho: O hloka chelete e ngata ho etsa tekanyetso — HA SE NNETE! E sebetsa ka chelete efe kapa efe.

misconceptions.english: Budgeting means cutting all fun — FALSE! It means intentional spending.
misconceptions.sesotho: Tekanyetso e bolela ho kgaola boithabiso bohle — HA SE NNETE! E bolela ho sebedisa ka boomo.

misconceptions.english: No need to budget if you do not overspend — FALSE! Budgets optimize savings.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ha ho hlokahale tekanyetso haeba o sa sebedise ho feta — HA SE NNETE! Tekanyetso e ntlafatsa poloko.

misconceptions.english: Budgeting apps are necessary — FALSE! A notebook works fine.
misconceptions.sesotho: Di-app tsa tekanyetso di a hlokahala — HA SE NNETE! Buka ya ho ngola e sebetsa hantle.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to create your first budget?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho etsa tekanyetso ya hao ya pele?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we practice dividing M100 into categories?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re ikwetlise ho arola M100 ka dikarolo?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to learn about tracking expenses?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho ithuta ho latela ditshenyehelo?
Na o batla ho tseba molao wa 50/30/20?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about saving money too?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue le ka ho boloka chelete?

how_to.english: Divide your money into Spend, Save, and Give.
how_to.sesotho: Arola chelete ka Sebedisa, Boloka le Fana.

how_to.english: Use three jars or envelopes for your money.
how_to.sesotho: Sebedisa linkho kapa di-enfelopo tse tharo.

how_to.english: Write down what you want to buy and check if you have enough.
how_to.sesotho: Ngola seo o batlang ho se reka mme o hlahlobe.

how_to.english: List all income and expenses for one month.
how_to.sesotho: Ngola moputso le ditshenyehelo tsohle tsa kgwedi.

how_to.english: Adjust spending to not exceed income.
how_to.sesotho: Fetola tshebediso ho se fete moputso.

how_to.english: Use zero-based budgeting or the 50/30/20 rule.
Track every Maloti and review monthly.
how_to.sesotho: Latela Maloti a mang le a mang kgwedi le kgwedi.

how_to.english: Build an emergency fund into your budget.

why.english: A budget helps you know where your money goes.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e o thusa ho tseba moo chelete e yang.

why.english: Budgeting helps you save for things you want.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e thusa ho bolokela dintho tseo o di batlang.

why.english: A budget stops you from running out of money.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e thibela ho felloa ke chelete.
Tekanyetso e thibela ho sebedisa ho feta le sekoloto.

why.english: A budget helps you achieve financial goals.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e thusa ho fihlela dipakane.

why.english: Budgeting gives you control over your money.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e o fa taolo hodima chelete.
Tekanyetso e ntlafatsa ho arola mehlodi.

why.english: A budget provides visibility into cash flow.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso e fana ka ponahalo ya phallo.

why.english: Budgeting is the foundation of financial planning.
why.sesotho: Tekanyetso ke motheo wa moralo wa lichelete.

situation.english: Palesa has M30. She needs bread (M10) and wants sweets (M25). Can she buy both?
situation.sesotho: Palesa o na le M30. O hloka bohobe (M10) mme o batla dipompong (M25). A ka reka ka bobeli?

advice.english: Bread + sweets = M35. She needs M5 more. She should prioritise bread (need) over sweets (want).
advice.sesotho: Bohobe + dipompong = M35. O hloka M5 e nngwe. O lokela ho beha bohobe (tlhoko) pele ho dipompong (takatso).

lesson.english: Needs come before wants when budgeting.
lesson.sesotho: Ditlhoko di tla pele ho ditakatso.

situation.english: Tumelo earns M500 monthly. Expenses: transport M150, food M200, airtime M50, entertainment M150. Total = M550. What should change?
situation.sesotho: Tumelo o fumana M500. Ditshenyehelo: dipalangwang M150, dijo M200, airtime M50, boithabiso M150. Kakaretso = M550. Ho lokela ho fetoha eng?

advice.english: He overspends by M50. Cut entertainment from M150 to M100.
advice.sesotho: O sebedisa M50 ho feta. Fokotsa boithabiso ho tloha M150 ho ya M100.

lesson.english: When expenses exceed income, reduce wants first.
lesson.sesotho: Ha ditshenyehelo di feta moputso, fokotsa ditakatso pele.

situation.english: A student has M3,000 monthly. Fixed: rent M1,200, utilities M300, food M800. Variable: transport M300, entertainment M300. What is the savings potential?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o na le M3,000. E sa fetoheng: rente M1,200, motlakase M300, dijo M800. E fetohang: dipalangwang M300, boithabiso M300. Poloko e ka ba bokae?

advice.english: Total expenses = M2,900. Savings potential = M100. Reduce entertainment to M200 to save M200.
advice.sesotho: Kakaretso = M2,900. Poloko = M100. Fokotsa boithabiso ho M200 ho boloka M200.

lesson.english: Small adjustments in variable expenses increase savings.
lesson.sesotho: Diphetoho tse nyane ditshenyehelong di eketsa poloko.
